blocks.raw: <ArticleMedia id="media-law012-liability-comparison" layout="single" variant="contained" type="image" status="placeholder" aspectRatio="16:9" title="Article 1723 vs Quasi-Delict vs Contractual Liability" alt="Comparison diagram showing the three liability frameworks: Article 1723 (strict liability, structural collapse, 15+10 year timeline), Quasi-Delict Article 2176 (negligence-based, any damage, 4-year prescription), and Contractual liability Article 1144 (breach of written contract, 10-year prescription)." placementIntent="legal-framework" suggestedSearchQuery="Article 1723 quasi-delict Article 2176 comparison Philippines architect liability" replacementNotes="Create a three-column comparison. Column 1: Article 1723 — Strict liability, structural collapse only, requires contractual relationship, 15-year exposure + 10-year post-collapse, solidary for construction defects. Column 2: Quasi-Delict (Art 2176-2194) — Negligence-based, any damage including non-collapse, applies without contract, 4-year prescription, third parties can sue. Column 3: Contractual (Art 1144) — Breach of written contract, 10-year prescription. Bottom section: 'Can proceed concurrently — not mutually exclusive.'" suggestedAsset="Diagram or reference image" alt="Four-element negligence proof: duty, breach, causation, damages" caption="Future diagram: four-element negligence proof: duty, breach, causation, damages" />
